instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Pat them very dry with a clean towel. Transfer them to a bowl and toss with the olive oil, cumin, garlic powder, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, 1 tsp salt and the pepper.

Spread the chickpeas in a single layer on the sheet. Roast for 25 minutes, shaking the pan every 8 minutes, until they're golden and crisp. Let them cool for a few minutes. Taste one. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Meanwhile, make the sauce. Juice the lemon into a bowl. Add the tahini, dill, a pinch of salt and the garlic, minced. Whisk, adding 1/4 cup water a splash at a time, until you can pour it.
Slice the tomatoes. Thinly slice half the red onion. Chop 1/4 cup parsley.
Warm the pitas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 seconds on each side. Cut them in half and open each half into a pocket.
Fill each pocket with the chickpeas, tomato, onion and parsley, then drizzle the sauce over the top.

To pack for lunch, keep the chickpeas, the sauce and the vegetables in separate containers and fill the pitas when you eat. The chickpeas and sauce keep in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. Eat the chickpeas cold or reheat them on a sheet pan at 400°F for 5 minutes.
method_notes: My Cooking Journey (5 from 21 ratings) roasts the chickpeas at 400°F with cumin, coriander and garlic, and serves them in pita with a tahini sauce and a chopped tomato, onion and parsley salad. Minimalist Baker (4.93 from 94) adds cinnamon, paprika and a dill and garlic sauce on hummus or tahini, and Love and Lemons (4.91 from 40) uses a yogurt sauce and zhoug. This version keeps the lead's tahini sauce without its yogurt so it stays dairy-free, and takes the spice mix and roasting time from Minimalist Baker. Amounts are scaled for four wraps.
